title: Citric Acid Cycle and Related Intermediates Extraction Protocol
author: Henri Brunengraber
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ydbfs2n

steps.title: Weigh frozen tissue
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.1–0.5 g of powdered frozen tissue (stored at –80 °C) into a pre‑weighed, tarred 15 mL conical tube that has been chilled over dry ice, and record the exact tissue weight.

steps.title: Add internal standards
steps.instruction: Spike the powdered tissue with the selected internal standards: approximately 50 nM [¹³C₆]citrate, ~30 nM [¹³C₄]succinate, and optionally ~30 nM (RS)-3‑hydroxy[²H₅]glutarate.

steps.title: Homogenize in acid buffer
steps.instruction: Add 3–5 mL of 5 % acetic acid in methanol/water (1:1) extraction buffer (chilled on ice) to the tube and homogenize the tissue for 2 min on an ice bath.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the homogenate at 670 × g for 30 min at 4 °C. Decant the supernatant into a glass test tube, keep it on ice, and process immediately (or freeze at –80 °C until GC‑MS analysis).

steps.title: Aliquot for derivatization
steps.instruction: Pipette 100–200 µL of the collected supernatant into a new test tube. If parallel lipid, cholesterol, or acyl‑CoA analysis is planned, use only 80 % of the supernatant. Add methoxylamine‑HCl if the target analytes contain keto groups, following the referenced procedure.

steps.title: Dry under nitrogen
steps.instruction: Dry the aliquoted sample completely under a stream of nitrogen gas.

steps.title: Derivatize with TMSC/TBDMS
steps.instruction: Add 70 µL of either TMSC or TBDMS derivatizing reagent (dissolved in a pyridine‑based solvent) to the dried sample and heat on a heating block at 80 °C for 1 hour (alternatively, react at room temperature overnight).

steps.title: Prepare for GC‑MS injection
steps.instruction: Transfer the derivatized sample to a GC insert, cap it, and set the GC‑MS instrument parameters as described in the references.

steps.title: GC‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the TMSC or TBDMS derivatives on an Agilent 5973N‑MSD coupled to an Agilent 6890 GC using a DB‑17MS capillary column (30 m × 0.25 mm × 0.25 µm; 60 m may be used). Operate the mass spectrometer in electron impact (EI) or ammonia chemical ionization (CI) mode with selective ion monitoring (SIM) of the m/z values for each analyte; when stable‑isotope‑labeled standards are used, monitor the M0–M+ m/z series.
